title: What Savitri told Death
hookLine: Savitri has no weapon on the road behind Death, only words about the company of the good
carry: satsang: time near the good is never wasted
last: A VRATA: A FAST HELD AS PRAYER FOR SOMEONE.

cards: No sword. No army. No spell.
When Yama, the lord of death, draws Satyavan's life out of his body and turns south, Savitri has nothing to fight with. What she has is a voice.
She walks behind Death and talks, and again and again, Death stops to listen. Last year we followed the boons one by one. Today we listen to what she actually says, because that's what moves him.

teach.b: Yama tells her to turn back. Her first answer is about where she belongs: where her husband is taken, she goes. Then she speaks of friendship.

The wise say, she tells him, that walking seven steps together makes people friends, and she has walked more than that beside him. She doesn't plead with Death as an enemy. She claims him as a companion on the road.
Then she speaks of dharma, and of the good, the people who keep to it. Yama is pleased and offers a gift, anything but Satyavan's life. She asks for her father-in-law's sight.

teach.h: NEAR THE GOOD IS NEVER WASTED
teach.b: She keeps talking: being near the good, even for a moment, is never wasted. Another gift: her father-in-law's kingdom. The good are kind even to those who wrong them, she says.
Another gift: sons for her own father. And the good, she says, hold the world up by their truth. Each time, what pleases Yama is not grief and not cleverness.
It's what she says about goodness.

teach.h: SATSANG: THE COMPANY OF THE GOOD
teach.b: Here's the teaching she's pointing at, one Hindus prize: satsang, the company of the good. Being near holy and good people is held to change you, slowly, the way sitting near a fire warms you.

It's why Hindus gather at the temple for bhajans and talks, why families sit together for a reading, why a visit to a holy person is called a blessing. This is a week's end, so look back. Kunti walked into vanaprastha.
Gandhari blessed dharma over her own side, bound her eyes, and poured water for her sons.
Savitri, named for the Gayatri, kept a vow, and now speaks of the good to Death himself.

how: Hindus gather for satsang, the company of the good, at temples and in homes, for bhajans, readings and talks; Savitri's words to Yama are heard when her story is retold, and on the day of the vow some married women keep in her name.

o: a wife whose talk of the good moved Death to give
a wife who begged Death in tears to spare him
a wife who fought Death's servants with a sword

games.q: what Savitri says, and what Yama gives — tap the pairs.
p: never wasted, even for a moment
given back his sight, then his kingdom

s: Savitri wins Satyavan back by fighting Yama
she has no weapon; she walks behind him and talks.
what pleases Yama, each time, is what she says about the good
she speaks of dharma and the good, and he keeps offering gifts.
satsang means you can only pray alone
it's time spent with good and holy people: Savitri says even a moment of it is never wasted.

games.q: you're walking behind Death, and he tells you to turn back. what do you say first?
o: beg him to take you instead.
tell him where your husband goes, you go, and call him a friend.
games.why: she says she goes where her husband is taken, and that seven steps together make people friends. Death stops to listen.

practice: Call to mind someone whose goodness you've seen up close, not well-known, just good, and one small kind thing they did that nobody else noticed.
Sit near them in your mind for a few breaths, the way Savitri says the good are worth being near, and let a little of it rub off.
If you pray, you can give thanks for them; this week, you might find a way to spend real time near them.

wordCard.voice: Savitri. The woman who walked behind Death and spoke about the good until he gave her what she asked. Today's word.

orig.note: Sanskrit: the princess's name, the same as the goddess who granted her birth and the verse to the sun god Savitr.

carryVoice: Your line: satsang, time near the good is never wasted. Savitri told Death so. Same time tomorrow.

sources.ref: Mahabharata, Vana Parva, Pativrata-mahatmya Parva (Savitri follows Yama; seven steps and friendship; her speeches on dharma and the good; the boons for her father-in-law and father)
